title: Fusion decision synthesis and benchmark protocol
content:
Purpose:
This doc synthesizes a repeatable decision protocol and benchmark harness for choosing when to prefer fused attention kernels vs paged/flash variants for our inference runtime. It contains the measurement protocol, the hypothesis matrix we used, representative result excerpts, and a short set of actionable rules for runtime routing. This is a working note intended to consolidate hands-on experiments (low ceremony) and provide a baseline that Solutions/Serving can reproduce and extend.

Context / motivation:
- We frequently observe non-monotonic latency across sequence-length mixes and batch sizes when switching between (1) native FlashAttention builds (Flash2), (2) our paged-attn implementation that shards KV to host memory for large context, and (3) a family of fused-MHA+mmap kernels that try to fuse qkv+attn+project.
- Prior retrospective notes scattered across the team (traces, perf logs, ad-hoc scripts) made triage slow. We need a compact benchmark protocol and a simple decision tree so the runtime can pick a kernel at request time with predictable cost/latency tradeoffs.

Goals:
1) Define an automated, low-friction microbenchmark protocol for kernel selection that covers the dominant customer workload mixes in production (seq len distribution, batch mix, concurrency).
2) Produce a small set of rules (heuristics + thresholds) that map workload features -> kernel choice.
3) Surface pathological operating points where fusion/regression risk is high (i.e., fused kernel slower than Flash at long sequences or small batches).
4) Deliver artifact links and example harness so SRE/Perf can re-run.

Hypotheses to test (short):
H1: Fused-MHA kernels outperform Flash2 at medium seq lengths (512-2048) for large batch sizes (>=8 on A100) because they reduce per-token kernel launches and memory traffic.
H2: Flash2 wins for small-batch, medium-long sequences due to lower memory amplification and better tensorcore packing at those shapes.
H3: Paged-attention becomes necessary when persistent KV exceeds GPU memory (~available_mem - 12GB on our nodes) and fusion decisions must defer to paged variant to avoid OOMs or catastrophic thrashing.
H4: Kernel handoffs cause tail-latency spikes during warmups; a short rolling warmup window (50 requests) mitigates stutter.

Experiment matrix (protocol):
- Hardware: A100-40GB (p3dn-like), H100-80GB (prod staging), and one small T4 instance for edge comparisons. Report chip, driver, cuda, cuDNN, and torch/flash version.
- Model: Llama2-13B (FP16), and a distilled 7B variant for smaller memory curves. Use compiled model artifacts we ship in /artifacts/benchmarks.
- Kernel variants (tagged in harness): flash2, paged-attn, fused-qkv-attn, fused-mha-v2 (experimental). Each variant should have a reproducible env: git sha + build flags.
- Sequence length profiles: {prompt-heavy: 64/128/256}, {mid: 512/1024}, {long: 2048/4096}. For production realism sample sequence lengths from our request histograms (see linked artifact INF-3245).
- Batch sizes: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16] with synthetic batching and with real coalescing enabled (simulate runtime coalescer).
- KV-cache mode: cold (first-forward only), warm (representative subsequent tokens), and mixed (50% cold, 50% warm).
- Concurrency: single-stream, multi-stream (4, 8 concurrent streams) with interleaving arrival times to simulate microbursts.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency per request (end-to-end and kernel-only), tokens/sec, GPU SM utilization, L2 hit ratios (if available), memory high-water mark, OOMs, and variance (stddev) of per-token latency. Also record NVTX traces and profiler samples for cross-correlation.

Harness and measurement hygiene:
- Each point: run for 120s steady-state after a short 20s warmup for fused kernels; repeat 5 runs and record median. For p99/stability analysis run a 15-minute long-run for selected operating points.
- Isolate background noise: pin CPU affinity for harness threads, disable telemetry that causes extra NVML noise during a single-run experiment, and ensure no other pods are on the GPU.
- Use deterministic RNG seeds for input token inputs where possible to reduce variance due to attention mask branching.
- Collect raw traces (nvprof/nvtx/torch-trt traces) and a small flamegraph per-kernel to inspect launch counts and memory copies.

Representative findings (excerpt from runs on A100-40GB, Llama2-13B fp16):
- Mid sequences (512) at batch 8: fused-qkv-attn showed 12% better tokens/sec than flash2, and kernel launch counts dropped ~35%. p90 latency reduced by ~10%.
- Small batch (1-2), sequence 512: flash2 consistently better (p99 ~20ms lower) because fused kernel failed to saturate tensorcores due to underfilled warps.
- Long sequences (2048+), fused kernels regressed: memory transient increases led to L2 thrashing and 30% higher p99 than flash2 for batch sizes <=4.
- Paged-attn was only viable for contexts larger than ~45k tokens combined KV; below that the paging overhead added ~8-15% latency compared to flash2. Once beyond GPU RAM, paged-attn avoided OOM and had stable albeit higher latency.
- Warm/cold behavior: fused kernels had higher cold-start latency (kernel caching and memory allocs). A 50-request rolling warmup reduced median and p99 by ~7-9% in steady traffic.

Short decision rules (v0):
1) If persistent KV > available_gpu_margin (empirically 12GB), route -> paged-attn.
2) Else if batch_size >= 8 and seq_mode in [512, 1024] and concurrency <= 4 -> prefer fused-qkv-attn.
3) Else if batch_size <= 2 or seq_mode <= 256 -> prefer flash2.
4) For seq_length >= 2048 prefer flash2 unless fused kernel has explicit long-seq microbenchmarks showing better p99 on that GPU/driver combo.
5) Always keep a runtime fallback: if chosen kernel reports growing p95 delta > 20% over baseline for 1 minute, switch to alternate variant and mark replicate for alerting.

Open observations / unknowns:
- H100 behavior is different: fused kernels sometimes outperform at longer seqs due to improved WMMA shapes; we need a consolidated H100 matrix (this doc only contains A100 excerpts).
- Driver and CUDA minor versions cause up to 6% variance in intense memory traffic cases. We should pin test images in CI.
- Effects of fragmentation on long-lived models with KV churn: need long-run (24h) tests.

Artifacts shipped with this note (how to reproduce):
- bench harness: github PR linked above (serving-runtime/bench/harness/kernel_select_bench). See README in PR for env.
- sample NVTX traces: s3://redwood-bench/attn/kernel_select/2025-11-18/{flash2,fused, paged}/<files>.tgz
- run script: scripts/run_matrix.sh - refers to docker image sha: registry.redwood.io/bench/kernel-select:sha-2b5d.

Next steps (action items):
- Marco: add H100 runs and paste results into the confluence decision page (due 2025-12-08).
- Janelle: add CI job that runs the microbenchmark on every fused kernel PR and publishes a one-line delta vs baseline. (INF-3245 assigned).
- Owen: instrument runtime to capture the new runtime metric 'kernel_selection_penalty' (p95 delta over baseline) and emit to tracing.
- Me (Asha): finalize this note into the confluence decision tree and add example config JSON for runtime routing.

Risks / caveats:
- These heuristics are empirical and tied to our build flags and kernel versions. Many edge cases exist (multi-tenant noisy nodes, memory fragmentation) that can flip ordering. Treat this as the first-pass policy and keep fallbacks in code.
- Reproducing exact numbers requires pinned images and quiet hardware. Expect +/- 8% variance across runs.

Appendix (quick reproducible commands):
- run single point: ./bench/run_point.sh --kernel fused-qkv-attn --batch 8 --seq 512 --model Llama2-13B --gpus 1 --reps 5
- collect nvtx: ./bench/collect_nvtx.sh --out /tmp/traces --duration 300
- analyze: python tools/compute_summary.py --inputs /tmp/results/*.json --output /tmp/summary.json

Reviewers asked: Marco Ruiz, Janelle Kim, Owen Brooks, Priya Nambiar (SRE)

Notes to self (unfinished):
- Add a small table of exact p50/p95/p99 numbers per kernel for the most common production mixes.
- Add comparison vs CPU fallback for tiny-medium models (7b) running on T4s for edge customers.

(End of working note)
